The party primaries were held on August 9, 2022. Incumbent [[Republican Party of Wisconsin|Republican]] Senator [[Ron Johnson]] won election to a third term, defeating [[Democratic Party of Wisconsin|Democratic]] [[Lieutenant Governor of Wisconsin|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Mandela Barnes]]{{cite news |last1=Edelman |first1=Adam |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Ron Johnson defeats Mandela Barnes in Wisconsin Senate race, NBC News projects |publisher=NBC News |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/ron-johnson-defeats-mandela-barnes-wisconsin-senate-race-nbc-news-proj-rcna54938 |access-date=9 November 2022}} by 26,718 votes—a one-point margin of victory. In this election, Johnson won five counties he lost in 2016, while his overall victory margin decreased from both 2010 and 2016. In 2016, Johnson had pledged to serve only two terms in the Senate. He reversed this decision in 2022.{{cite news |title=Source: U.S. Sen. Ron Johnson to run for reelection |website=wisn.com |url=https://www.wisn.com/article/source-ron-johnson-to-run-for-re-election/38697598 |access-date=January 7, 2022}} The race was one of the most competitive of the cycle, and it followed considerable Democratic success in recent statewide elections. In [[2018 Wisconsin elections|2018]], Democrats won every statewide contest on the ballot, including the election for the state's [[2018 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|other Senate seat]]. This was one of the two Republican-held Senate seats up for election in a state that [[Joe Biden]] won in the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]].{{cite web |last=Greenwood |first=Max |date=January 1, 2021 |title=Seven Senate Races to Watch in 2022 |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/530880-seven-senate-races-to-watch-in-2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210101120928/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/530880-seven-senate-races-to-watch-in-2022 |archive-date=January 1, 2021 |access-date=January 1, 2021 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |language=en}} Barnes led in most polls during the summer of 2022. In the final weeks prior to the election, Johnson took a lead of more than three points in the polling average. Though Johnson ultimately prevailed, this election was the closest of his three Senate victories. This was the first Senate election in Wisconsin since [[1998 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|1998]] in which the winning candidate was of a [[split-ticket voting|different party]] than the winner of the [[2022 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|concurrent gubernatorial election]]. ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[Ron Johnson]], incumbent U.S. senator{{cite news |title=Source: U.S. Sen.
